title: The ZDX Score: scale, bands, score types and what lowers it

prose.text: The ZDX Score is the headline number of ZDX; the underlying probe metrics are the drill-down. {{represents}}

prose.label: Scale and bands.
prose.text: {{scale}} {{bands}} The MCP server's troubleshooting prompt uses other bands {{divergence:mcp-prompt-bands}}. The dashboards give the lowest score as 1 {{divergence:scale-range}}.

prose.label: On the user page.
prose.text: {{smooth-score}} {{root-cause-analysis}} {{root-cause-tier}} What the Factor values are is open {{gap:rca-details}}. {{compare-scores}} Which dashboards show the score is in [[zdx.dashboards]].

prose.label: Score types.
prose.text: {{score-types}} {{score-type-metrics}} An application's Real User Monitoring settings are part of its configuration, [[zdx.applications:rum-config]].

prose.label: How it is calculated.
prose.text: The 5-minute values, the hourly lows and the rollups per application, place, organization and user are in [[zdx.score.calculation]].

prose.label: Low scores.
prose.text: {{low-score-causes}} A Diagnostics Session can be started to troubleshoot a low score, [[zdx.diagnostics:low-scores]].

prose.label: Through the API.
prose.text: An API score of -1 means no data, not a bad score, and API values can differ slightly from the UI: [[shared.log-export.zdx:api-vs-ui]].

checks.do: Which score type the application is configured for (synthetic probes, Real User Monitoring or both) before comparing its score with another's.
Whether an API score of -1 is a no-data value rather than a poor score.

smooth-score.statement: In the ZDX Score Over Time graph on the user page the Smooth ZDX Score displays by default; it uses historical data to reduce short-term variations in the ZDX Score and provides a more representative metric with reduced variability, and the checkbox option under the graph shows the ZDX Score.

quotes: In the ZDX Score Over Time graph on the User page, the Smooth ZDX Score displays by default.
The Smooth ZDX Score uses historical data to reduce short-term variations in the ZDX Score and provides a more representative metric with reduced variability.
Select the checkbox option under the graph to view the ZDX Score.

root-cause-analysis.statement: For Poor scores that range from 0-33, the ZDX Score Over Time graph includes a feature to help identify reasons for the low score: the application tile with the lowest Poor score is preselected and ZDX runs root cause analysis automatically on the most recent Poor score, and Analyze Score or Analyze Range triggers potential factors for a point or a range. Each result gives a Factor (a probable cause), an Explanation and a Confidence Level based on probes with similar issues; automated analysis for Poor scores is not applicable to Call Quality applications.

quotes: For Poor scores that range from 0–33, the ZDX Score Over Time graph includes a feature to help identify reasons for the low score.
The application tile with the lowest Poor score is preselected, and ZDX runs root cause analysis automatically on the most recent Poor score.
Automated analysis for Poor ZDX Scores is not applicable to ZDX Call Quality applications.
Factor: Shows a probable cause for the low score.
Explanation: Addresses why the corresponding factor might be the issue.
Confidence Level: Quantifies the assumed accuracy of the analysis, based on probes with similar issues.
click Analyze Score within the tooltip to, again, trigger potential factors that might have contributed to the score.
Click Analyze Range to display potential factors that might have contributed to the low scores within your specified time range.

root-cause-tier.statement: In the subscription table, Root Cause Analysis is not supported on Standard and Microsoft 365 and supported on Advanced and Advanced Plus.

quotes: | Root Cause Analysis | Not supported | Not supported | Supported | Supported |
| Feature | Standard | Microsoft 365 | Advanced | Advanced Plus |

compare-scores.statement: Comparing ZDX Scores uses web, device and Cloud Path metrics to help determine differences in scoring. A point can be compared with the last known good score, which searches the score history for the last available score between 66 and 100, with the same time on the previous day, 2 days or 7 days, or with a future score up to the current date and time; web metrics are not used or provided when comparing scores for a Network application.

quotes: The feature utilizes web, device, and Cloud Path metrics to help determine differences in scoring.
The option for Last known good score searches the score history for the last available score between 66 and 100.
The time range options show the score from the same time on the previous day, 2 days, or 7 days.
Compare the ZDX Score of your selected point to a future ZDX Score, up to the current date and time.
Web metrics are not used or provided when comparing scores for a Network application.

represents.statement: A ZDX Score represents all users in the organization, across all applications, locations and cities; it appears on the Admin Console dashboards that show Digital Experience metrics and adjusts to the time period and filters selected there.

quotes: A ZDX Score represents all users in your organization, across all applications, all locations, and all cities.
You can see the score on the Zscaler Admin Console dashboards that capture Digital Experience (ZDX) metrics.
Depending on the time period and filters selected within the dashboards, the score adjusts accordingly.

scale.statement: The ZDX Score runs from 0 (lowest) to 100 (highest); the lowest numbers indicate a Poor score and the highest a Good score.

quotes: The ZDX Score is based on a scale of 0 (lowest) to 100 (highest) with the lowest numbers indicating a Poor score and the highest numbers indicating a Good score.

bands.statement: A score falls in one of three categories: Good, 66 to 100, green; Okay, 34 to 65, amber; Poor, 0 to 33, red.

quotes: Good: The score is above an acceptable threshold and ranges from 66-100. The color for this range is green.
Okay: The score is acceptable and ranges from 34-65. The color for this range is amber.
Poor: The score is below an acceptable threshold and ranges from 0-33. The color for this range is red.

low-score-causes.statement: The help attributes low scores often to the network or local environment, listing device issues (restarts, CPU in use), connection issues (Wi-Fi signal strength), slow applications and high network latency (Wi-Fi, home network, ISP) as potential reasons.

quotes: Low scores can often be attributed to underlying issues related to the network or local environment.
Issues with a user's device (e.g., restarts, amount of CPU in use, etc.).
Issues with the connection (e.g., Wi-Fi signal strength).
- Slow applications.
High latency on the network (e.g., Wi-Fi, home network, ISP).

score-types.statement: There are two ZDX Score types and one combined type, depending on how applications are configured: the Synthetic Probe Score measured with Cloud Path or Web probes, the RUM Score measured with Real User Monitoring, and the Combined Score of both; they can differ because they use different configurations and metrics.

quotes: There are two different ZDX Score types and one combined ZDX Score type depending on how you configure your applications to measure ZDX Score:
Synthetic Probe Score: The score is measured using probes (i.e., Cloud Path probe or Web probe).
RUM Score: The score is measured using Real User Monitoring (RUM).
Combined Score: The score is a combination of both Synthetic Probe Score and RUM Score.
These scores can differ from each other as they use different application configurations and use different metrics

score-type-metrics.statement: In the help's table, Web probe metrics (Page Fetch Time, Server Response Time, DNS Time, Availability) and Cloud Path metrics (End-to-End latency, Packet Loss, Hops, Packet Count) count toward the Synthetic Probe Score with a probe-only configuration, the RUM Score with a RUM-only configuration and both scores with combined configurations; web browser metrics (Page Views, Route Changes, Page Load Time, Core Web Vitals) are not used with a probe-only configuration and otherwise count toward the RUM Score.

quotes: | Metrics | Synthetic Probe Configuration Only | RUM Configuration Only | Combined Configurations |
| Web probe metrics: Page Fetch Time Server Response Time DNS Time Availability | Synthetic Probe Score | RUM Score | Both Scores |
| Cloud Path probe metrics for network performance: End-to-End latency Packet Loss Hops Packet Count | Synthetic Probe Score | RUM Score | Both Scores |
| Web browser metrics: Page Views Route Changes Page Load Time Core Web Vitals | N/A | RUM Score | RUM Score |

rca-details.title: What the root cause Factor values are and whether the console analysis is the API's score analysis
rca-details.detail: The console's Factor values and how the Confidence Level is computed are not listed, and no source says whether the console analysis is the API's score analysis job, [[zdx.diagnostics.analysis:contract-result]]. The Smooth ZDX Score is described with no window or method.
rca-details.blocks: explaining a root cause result or reproducing it through the API

scale-range.summary: The lowest ZDX Score: the score article gives the scale as 0 (lowest) to 100, while the Performance Dashboard, the Applications Overview and the Users Overview give it as 1 to 100, and the Performance Dashboard also gives the Poor band as 0 to 33.

quotes: The ZDX Score is based on a scale of 0 (lowest) to 100 (highest) with the lowest numbers indicating a Poor score and the highest numbers indicating a Good score.
The ZDX Score is based on a scale of 1 (lowest) to 100 (highest), with the lowest numbers indicating a poor score and highest numbers indicating a good score.
Poor: The score is below an acceptable threshold and ranges from 0–33.

positions.says: The scale runs from 1 (lowest) to 100 (highest), yet the same page gives the Poor band as 0 to 33.

quotes: ZDX Score: The application's ZDX Score from 1 to 100, with 1 being the lowest and 100 being the highest.

positions.says: An application's ZDX Score runs from 1 to 100.

quotes: The ZDX Score column shows the user's ZDX Score from 1–100, with 1 being the lowest and 100 being the highest.

positions.says: A user's ZDX Score runs from 1 to 100.

scale-range.impact: Whether a score of 0 can occur is not settled by the help; the pages that say 1 also give a Poor band starting at 0.

mcp-prompt-bands.summary: The score bands: the help and the Python SDK's `score_bucket` docstring use Good 66-100, Okay 34-65 and Poor 0-33; the MCP server's ZDX troubleshooting prompt tells the agent 80-100 Good, 50-79 Degraded and 0-49 Poor.

quotes: Good: The score is above an acceptable threshold and ranges from 66-100. The color for this range is green.
Okay: The score is acceptable and ranges from 34-65. The color for this range is amber.
Poor: The score is below an acceptable threshold and ranges from 0-33. The color for this range is red.

positions.says: The `score_bucket` values map to poor 0-33, okay 34-65 and good 66-100.

quotes: - Score bands: 80-100 = Good, 50-79 = Degraded, 0-49 = Poor.

mcp-prompt-bands.impact: An agent following the MCP prompt calls a score of 70 Degraded where the console shows Good, and a 40 Poor where the console shows Okay, and its bands do not line up with the `score_bucket` filter.
